resources.string: Measurement methodology
Plan a representative fleet study, calculate a sample and interpret technical resource shortages separately from business availability.
Open methodology and calculator
Two usage modes

Local mode describes one device: inspect its current readings, history and diagnostic sources. Fleet mode estimates whether groups of corporate devices have enough capacity for defined work scenarios. In fleet mode AHWOTel records each selected device and OTLP can deliver measurements to a collector for joint analysis. The APK does not by itself select devices or make a fleet-wide business verdict.
Study workflow

1. Define a business scenario and its active working hours.
2. Define the target device population and homogeneous groups.
3. Select devices randomly or by a documented representative procedure.
4. Measure the same scenario and configuration.
5. Convert technical signals into resource-insufficiency intervals.
6. Compare the union of those intervals with an approved business allowance.
7. Report uncertainty, data coverage and differences between groups before concluding whether capacity is sufficient.
Representative groups

Do not mix materially different scenarios into one sample. Separate strata can be required for device model, Android or OEM build, RAM/storage class, managed profile, application version, network environment, shift and business workflow. Calculate and recruit a sample for every stratum that needs a separate conclusion. Thousands of repeated readings from one phone improve its time series but do not replace independent devices in a fleet sample.
Sample-size calculator

Proportion mode estimates a device share, for example the share that exceeded a business allowance. Mean mode estimates an average, for example average resource-insufficiency minutes per shift. Population correction is applied. The reserve compensates for devices that do not produce usable data.

What counts as technical resource insufficiency

Define the rule before collecting data and preserve it with the study. A threshold is evidence that an agreed technical condition occurred, not proof of its root cause and not automatically a business outage. Use sustained intervals rather than isolated samples.
Combined Performance State

A practical primary event can be performance.state ≥ 2 (Degraded or Critical) after the configured escalation/recovery filter. Level 1 can be reported as warning rather than shortage. Performance State is the maximum of the available CPU, memory, storage and thermal pressure assessments; missing inputs make the assessment partial. Thresholds belong to the session and can differ from current settings.
CPU examples

performance.pressure.cpu ≥ 2 is a direct configured shortage condition when device.cpu.utilization is readable. Default CPU candidates are 80% / 90% / 95%, but they are examples and must be validated against the workload. agent.cpu.runqueue_wait and agent.scheduling.delay show that AHWOTel work waited to run; rising values can support a CPU-contention hypothesis when aligned with workload latency, but cannot alone prove that the whole device lacked CPU. If system CPU is UNSUPPORTED, these indirect signals do not turn it into a measured utilization value.
Memory examples

performance.pressure.memory ≥ 2, Android low-memory indication (device.memory.low = 1), or a sustained low device.memory.available_percent rule can define insufficiency. A policy such as “RAM use must not exceed 60%” is equivalent to “available RAM must remain at least 40%”; it can be a corporate criterion but is not an AHWOTel default or a universal Android threshold. Default available-RAM candidates are 15% / 10% / 5%. Correlate with app restarts, reclaim or business latency where those data exist.
Storage and I/O examples

performance.pressure.storage ≥ 2 or sustained low device.storage.available_percent can define capacity insufficiency; default available-space candidates are 15% / 10% / 5%. device.storage.psi.* and device.storage.block.* counters can support an I/O-contention hypothesis when available with suitable privileges. There is no universal PSI or throughput threshold across flash types and OEM builds: establish a baseline for the same stratum and scenario.
Thermal examples

performance.pressure.thermal ≥ 2, sustained device.thermal.status or decreasing device.thermal.headroom can define a thermal-capacity event. With default candidates, Android thermal status 2 starts a degraded candidate. Thermal headroom is predictive and device-dependent. device.battery.temperature is the battery sensor; it is useful context but is not a CPU temperature and does not by itself prove CPU throttling.
Battery and operational availability

Low charge, no charging, battery health, voltage or temperature may explain operational unavailability such as a device that cannot finish a shift. They do not currently change Performance State automatically. If battery endurance is part of the business question, define it as a separate outcome, for example “completed an eight-hour shift without unplanned charging,” and analyse it alongside performance capacity.
Monitoring the monitor

agent.cpu.*, agent.memory.pss, agent.memory.rss and self-overhead metrics describe AHWOTel resource cost and measurement delay. Use them to show that the observer did not materially distort the scenario and to compare agent versions. They measure the monitoring process, not total device capacity. A high agent value requires investigation and cannot be counted as device insufficiency without a predefined rule and supporting device evidence.
Intervals and missing data

Apply the configured escalation and recovery windows, then merge overlapping CPU, memory, storage and thermal intervals before summing unavailable time; otherwise one minute with two simultaneous shortages is counted twice. UNSUPPORTED, permission denied, disabled collection, stale values and gaps are unknown coverage—not Normal and not a shortage. Report measured working time and unknown time with every result.
Business decision examples

Aggregate only inside defined working windows. Useful outputs include: share of devices with any shortage; affected device-work-time; episode count; p50/p95 episode duration; and share exceeding a business allowance. Example policy: “capacity is sufficient if no more than 5% of devices have more than 10 merged minutes at Performance State ≥ 2 during a shift, with at least 90% measurement coverage.” These numbers are illustrative: the process owner must approve actual tolerances and the required confidence before measurement.
Interpretation limits

Association is not causation. Compare like-for-like groups, record configuration changes and investigate outliers. Report confidence intervals, not only point estimates. The calculator assumes independent representative devices and a normal approximation; it does not account for cluster sampling, repeated-measure correlation, weighting, multiple comparisons or selection bias. Use a statistician when the decision is high impact or these assumptions do not hold.
